description: Probe of the substrate-form hypothesis λ_scale = p(4)/2 − h²·G + O(h^4) for the Borromean baryon mass formula. Tests proton, neutron, Σ baryons, Λ baryon at MPFR 80 dps. Verifies the 5.6 ppm match for proton; solves for higher-order corrections; tests generation predictions (p(n)/2 for n=4,5,6); checks Skein S(B) interpretation. NO FITTING — all targets are computed from CODATA via the Borromean formula.

probe_2_neutron_common_form.interpretation: If λ has common substrate value 5/2 − h²·G + small, the p/n split lives in S(B) Skein. ΔS(n) - ΔS(p) should equal the Δm_pn ≈ 1.293 MeV / m_e.

probe_3_h4_correction.interpretation: c4 = +0.007510. Compare to simple candidates: if c4 ≈ G, then λ_p ≈ 5/2 − h²·G − h^4·G + O(h^6) = 5/2 − G·(h² + h^4 + ...) ≈ 5/2 − G·h²/(1−h²).

probe_4_generation_sigma.interpretation: If p(n)/2 generation hypothesis holds with p(5) = 7, λ_Σ_pred = 7/2 − h²·G = ~3.46. Observed Σ baryon λ values: Σ+ → 3.1183, Σ⁰ → 3.1269, Λ → 2.9251. Pattern fits IF λ_Σ is in the range 3.1 to 3.5; observed ~3.12 (Σ+), so prediction 3.46 is off by ~10%. Likely the generation hypothesis needs refinement OR Σ has additional Skein contribution.

probe_5_alternative_rationals.search: leading rational L close to 5/2, test L − h²·G vs λ_p

probe_6_Vol_B3_vs_8G.note: If Vol(B_3) = 8G exactly, the formula `λ = 5/2 − h²·G` becomes `λ = 5/2 − h²·Vol(B_3)/8`. The numerical values differ at the 7th decimal — likely the literature value's precision floor, not a structural difference. SnapPy high-precision computation would clarify.

probe_7_muon_sanity.interpretation: The muon has λ ≈ 1 by CAL-2 (definition of q_0). The Borromean formula does not apply to leptons; this is a sanity check that the 5/2 − h²·G value is NOT universal — it's specific to baryons with B_3 topology.

caveats: Probe-only — does not modify production compute paths. Findings inform the open R&D on λ_scale substrate derivation.
